title: RBAC roles/permissions for Optimization Config create/apply/promote/rollback (with audit + approvals requirements)
creator: Paula Mendes
description:
Context / why
Optimization Config changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles) have historically caused high-severity regressions when applied too broadly or by the wrong operator. Enterprise customers are explicitly asking for (1) strict RBAC around apply/rollback and (2) auditable approvals/change records.

This ticket defines the product requirements for RBAC roles/permissions, approval expectations, and auditability requirements for:
- create/version (drafting an Optimization Config version)
- validate (schema + semantic checks)
- apply (staged rollout/canary)
- promote (make version “active” for a scope)
- rollback (revert scope to a prior known-good version)

In scope
1) Permission model (RBAC) requirements
We need a minimal, understandable permission model that works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private, with sane defaults and supportability.

A. Resource and scope
- Resource: Optimization Config (versioned, immutable versions)
- Scope dimensions used in authorization decisions and auditing:
  - tenant (customer/org)
  - environment (prod/staging/dev where applicable; for Hosted treat as “prod” for customer traffic; for internal ops support multiple envs)
  - model (or model-family) optional
  - region optional
  - rollout object (canary job/controller) optional

B. Actions (fine-grained permissions)
Define explicit actions that can be mapped to roles:
- optimization_config.version.create
- optimization_config.version.read
- optimization_config.version.diff.read
- optimization_config.version.validate
- optimization_config.rollout.create (apply a version to a scope, including canary percentage)
- optimization_config.rollout.pause_resume
- optimization_config.rollout.abort
- optimization_config.promote (set version as active/pinned for scope after successful gates)
- optimization_config.rollback (revert scope to prior version)
- optimization_config.rollback.force (break-glass override for exceptional cases; see guardrails)
- optimization_config.approval.request
- optimization_config.approval.grant
- optimization_config.approval.read
- optimization_config.audit.read (read access to audit events in Console/API; not the ability to emit)

Notes:
- “validate” is a meaningful action because we don’t want arbitrary users spamming expensive semantic checks / eval harness runs.
- “rollback.force” is separated to ensure emergency-only use and stronger logging.

C. Required roles (minimum set)
We will ship with 4 baseline roles. Names can be adjusted but semantics must be clear.

1) Optimization Config Viewer
- Intended for: Support, Solutions Engineering, customer admins who need visibility.
- Can:
  - read versions + diffs + current active version by scope
  - read rollout status + history
  - read audit events related to optimization configs
- Cannot:
  - create, validate, apply, promote, rollback

2) Optimization Config Author
- Intended for: Applied ML / runtime engineers doing drafting, experimentation.
- Can:
  - create new versions (draft)
  - read versions/diffs
  - request validation and/or request approval (does not grant approval)
- Cannot:
  - apply to prod traffic scopes, promote, rollback
- Optional: can validate for non-prod scopes (configurable per org policy)

3) Optimization Change Operator
- Intended for: On-call/SRE/platform operators who execute controlled rollouts.
- Can:
  - validate (schema + semantic)
  - create rollouts (apply canary) for authorized scopes
  - pause/resume/abort rollouts
  - promote following successful gates AND required approvals
  - rollback following required approvals (or break-glass policy)
- Cannot:
  - grant approvals unless also assigned Approver role

4) Optimization Change Approver
- Intended for: “change management” approver group; for Redwood-managed Hosted/Dedicated this is typically SRE lead + platform lead; for customers this may be Customer Admin/Change Manager.
- Can:
  - grant approvals for apply/promote/rollback actions
  - view approval history
- Cannot:
  - execute rollout steps unless also Operator

D. Default policy recommendations (Hosted/Dedicated)
- Customer orgs:
  - Default to Viewer for most members.
  - Require explicit assignment for Operator/Approver.
  - For Dedicated + enterprise, recommend at least one Approver distinct from Operator (two-person rule) for prod scopes.
- Redwood internal ops:
  - Viewer broadly available.
  - Operator limited to on-call rotations (Platform Control Plane, SRE) and a small number of runtime leads.
  - Approver: SRE lead (Sean Gallagher) and designated Eng leads (Ethan Park, Mateo Alvarez delegates).

E. Private deployment policy recommendations
- Same roles, but enforcement occurs in the customer’s control plane deployment.
- Require a documented “break-glass” path: local admin can perform rollback.force but must be auditable (see Audit requirements below).

2) Approval requirements (product behavior)
Goal: Reduce accidental/bad changes without blocking incident response.

A. Approval objects
- An approval is a first-class record tied to:
  - action type (apply/promote/rollback/rollback.force)
  - target scope (tenant/model/region)
  - target version (or source+target versions for rollback)
  - requestor identity
  - approver identity (when granted)
  - timestamps
  - rationale

B. Required approvals by blast radius
Define blast radius tiers; implementation can start with a simple policy:
- Tier 0 (non-prod / staging): no approval required by default
- Tier 1 (prod, single region OR <= X% canary): 1 approval required
- Tier 2 (prod, multi-region OR > X% of traffic OR model-family-wide): 2 approvals required (two-person rule)

We can parameterize X in policy, default 10%.

C. Emergency rollback behavior
- Rollback should be fast, but controlled.
- Default requirement: 1 approval for rollback in prod.
- Break-glass: allow rollback.force without pre-approval ONLY for users with optimization_config.rollback.force, and require:
  - explicit “reason” string
  - incident ID (if available)
  - stronger audit event category + notification hooks

3) Audit logging requirements (what must be logged)
This ticket specifies what RBAC/approval actions must appear in audit logs and what fields must be present so enterprise customers can export to SIEM.

A. Events required
At minimum, must log:
- optimization_config.version.created
- optimization_config.version.validated
- optimization_config.rollout.started (apply)
- optimization_config.rollout.paused_resumed
- optimization_config.rollout.aborted
- optimization_config.version.promoted
- optimization_config.rollback.requested
- optimization_config.rollback.completed
- optimization_config.rollback.forced (if break-glass)
- optimization_config.approval.requested
- optimization_config.approval.granted
- rbac.role.assigned / rbac.role.revoked (if our product manages role bindings)
- authz.denied (for rollback/apply attempts) for troubleshooting (may be sampled/retained differently; see retention notes)

B. Required fields per event (minimum)
- event_name
- event_time
- actor (user/service principal), actor_type
- actor_org / tenant_id
- request_id / correlation_id
- action
- resource_type (optimization_config)
- resource_id (config_id) and config_version_id
- scope (tenant/model/region/environment) as tags
- rollout_id (if applicable)
- from_version_id / to_version_id (for rollback/promote where applicable)
- approval_id(s) referenced (if applicable)
- reason / change_summary (freeform string; required for rollback.force)
- client_ip and user_agent (Console/API)

C. Retention / access
- Customer-visible retention: match standard audit log retention offering; minimum 90 days for enterprise packages.
- Access controlled via optimization_config.audit.read.

4) Console UX requirements (what RBAC must enable)
- History page shows:
  - current active version per scope
  - version timeline with who/what/when
  - approvals status for apply/promote/rollback
- Rollback button visibility rules:
  - show disabled state with “insufficient permissions” and a link to required role, not a hard hide (to reduce support churn)
  - show “request approval” CTA if user is Operator but not Approver and approvals are required
- Confirmation modal must:
  - display blast radius summary
  - require reason text for rollback.force and optionally for normal rollback

Non-goals / explicitly out of scope (for PM-902)
- A full enterprise change-management workflow (CAB meetings, scheduled windows) beyond basic approval objects
- Fully automated, no-human rollback for all customers
- Cross-system transactional approvals spanning unrelated systems

Acceptance criteria
- Engineering can implement a policy bundle with the actions/roles above without ambiguity.
- Console behavior is consistent:
  - users without permissions see clear disabled states + instructions
  - approvals are required/enforced for the tiers defined
- Audit requirements are unblocked:
  - event list + required fields are sufficient for Security sign-off (Dr. Aisha Rahman)
  - ties cleanly into the audit log spec doc and SIEM export

Dependencies / related work
- ENG-4826 (emit audit log events for config lifecycle)
- ENG-4825 (rollback endpoint authz semantics)
- PM-901 (overall safe apply/rollback PRD)
- PM-904 (GA readiness checklist)
- rbac-policy-bundle PR to implement roles/actions (tracked in eng repo; see notes)

Links / references
- Confluence: Audit logging spec for optimization configs (event taxonomy + examples)
- ADR: safe apply gating signals (ties to promote permissions)
- GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle changes for optimization change permissions (implementation)

Open questions
1) Should “Author” be allowed to validate by default, or should validation always be Operator-only due to cost (eval runs)? Proposed default: Author can validate only for non-prod scopes; prod validation remains Operator-only.
2) Should rollback require 2 approvals for Tier 2 scopes? Proposed: yes, but allow rollback.force for emergency with strict audit + notifications.
3) For Private deployments: do we manage role bindings in product, or assume customer IdP/RBAC mapping? Proposed: support both; minimal requirement is we enforce roles at runtime and log role resolution in authz.denied.

Decision log
- 2025-10-11 (Paula Mendes + Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin): aligned on separating rollback.force permission and requiring reason/incident ID.
- 2025-10-17 (Sean Gallagher + Ethan Park): agreed on two-person rule for Tier 2 promotions; emergency rollback.force allowed for on-call with audit.

Latest update (2026-01-20)
- Implemented roles/actions in policy bundle; Console UX uses disabled-with-tooltip pattern and approval request CTA.
- Security sign-off pending final verification of audit fields in rollback events (tracked via ENG-4826).
